cases.query: I need a uniform guarantee that one finite quantum measurement never loses more output state distinguishability than another, even if the input is entangled with an external memory. The two possible preparations may give that memory different marginal states. Is there a finite reference-size test I can trust on arbitrary rational inputs?

source_use.statement: Given two finite quantum channels P,Q on a common quantum input, including measurement channels from POVMs, unrestricted complete relative-entropy comparison tests D[(P tensor id_R)(alpha)||(P tensor id_R)(beta)] >= D[(Q tensor id_R)(alpha)||(Q tensor id_R)(beta)] for EVERY finite untouched quantum reference R and EVERY joint input-state pair alpha,beta. Their reference marginals may differ. Here Umegaki D(A||B)=Tr[A(log A-log B)], with value +infinity when the support condition fails. For finite descriptions of rational-complex strictly positive POVM pairs on a common input,with variable input dimension and outcome counts,complete SLD dominance is coRE-complete and its failure is RE-complete. For every finite-dimensional channel pair,complete SLD order is equivalent to unrestricted complete Umegaki order over all finite references and all input-state pairs. No total computable function of a valid rational POVM pair bounds a reference dimension sufficient to witness every complete-SLD failure.

assumptions: Each test is finite-dimensional;dimensions are not bounded uniformly over inputs/tests.
Umegaki comparison permits every input-state pair;there is no equal-reference-marginal restriction.
No hardness conclusion for fixed input dimension,transpose-compatible subclasses,restricted-marginal entropy orders or numerical contraction coefficients.
The source-stated internal dependencies are included in Harjas's standing acceptance. N661 is separate context and is not promoted.
costs: Computable many-one reductions;finite symbolic construction,no efficiency or strategy/witness-acquisition guarantee.
Every failure has some finite witness;the result rules out a uniform computable sufficient dimension bound,not every restricted-case algorithm.
contract.obstruction: Permits programme reasoning from complete-order undecidability without imposing an unavailable computable ancilla cutoff or reopening the accepted proof. It supplies no physical implementation,novelty or practical-advantage evidence.
provides: An explicit two-channel comparison criterion on output distinguishability with arbitrary finite retained quantum memory, with no equal-reference-marginal restriction or subtraction of the memory entropy. This defines the requested relation; it is not an algorithm deciding it.
A programme-accepted generic-class undecidability premise and RE/coRE classification.
Equivalence with unrestricted complete Umegaki state-pair comparison.
No uniform total computable sufficient failure-reference cutoff from the rational POVM input.
requires: Two actual channels on the SAME quantum input; the joint input density matrices and untouched reference are allowed to be correlated. The generic computability classification additionally requires the stated rational-complex strictly positive POVM input class.
A common finite input;finite rational-complex strictly positive POVM descriptions for the computability classification.
For the equivalence,any finite-dimensional channel pair;all finite untouched references,faithful input baseline and traceless Hermitian tangent in SLD order.

cases.query: My two quantum channels are tested only after removing distinguishability already present in the untouched memory. How does this conditional comparison relate to the complete infinitesimal metric, and does it also give the unconstrained state-pair order?

source_use.statement: For arbitrary finite-dimensional quantum channels P,Q with the same input, the uniform conditional Umegaki relative-entropy order with constant c is equivalent to the complete equal-reference SLD metric order with the same c. Taking Q to be identity identifies the conditional Umegaki contraction coefficient with the complete equal-reference SLD coefficient.
